## jpegxl-rs.decision.c26-alias-mapping

### Revision 1 — C.2.6 alias mapping is symbols[u] = o, not 0

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.decision.c26-alias-mapping/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-entropy/**"` · topic `c26-alias-mapping`

In the C.2.6 alias-table build, symbols[u] = o (the overfull index), not 0. The
LaTeX renders it as 0, an OCR corruption; only o is consistent with the algorithm.
The invariant test (each symbol s appears exactly D[s] times across slots, offsets
a permutation of 0..D[s]) fails under = 0. If that test fires, the bug is in new
code, not the test.

**Context.** Recovered from HANDOFF "Already fixed" (2026-08-02).

## jpegxl-rs.decision.encoder-architecture-phases

### Revision 1 — Reorient encoder work to architecture phases 0-6 (outside-advice)

`active` · `@jpegxl-rs.decision.encoder-architecture-phases/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-cli/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-entropy/**"` · topic `encoder-architecture-phases`

After Opt-F through Opt-P leaf work, further leaf SIMD/LTO/PGO is deferred.
Implementation follows sources/outside-advice.md phases: (0) instrumentation
and matched-quality harness foundations; (1) output-preserving corrections;
(2) replace VarDCT quant/CfL unit of work; (3) replace candidate coefficient
retention with summaries; (4) rebuild modular planning; (5) perceptual
parity calibration; (6) entropy specialization and low-level opts last.
Phase completion is marked in AKR only. Clean-room boundary still forbids
porting libjxl architecture; behavioral comparison and black-box timing
remain allowed.

**Context.** Real-world benches showed ~15x VarDCT and ~30-100x Modular gaps with parallel+simd features already default-on. Flamegraphs and outside advice attribute the gap to call multiplicity and multi-pass planning, not missing AVX kernels on leaves that are already small fractions of wall time.

**Consequences.** jpegxl-rs.work.encoder-optimization-plan and Opt-* leaf milestones remain historical; new work items attach to architecture-phase work under this decision. sources/outside-advice.md is retained per policy.

## jpegxl-rs.decision.ledger-conventions

### Revision 1 — AKR ledger conventions for jpegxl-rs

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.decision.ledger-conventions/1` · scope `all` · topic `ledger-conventions`

The AKR ledger at the repository root is the plan-of-record. One namespace,
jpegxl-rs; structure comes from scope path globs over JPXL/crates/**, not from
extra namespaces. Kind crosswalk from the retired markdown: roadmap phases and
milestones become milestone and track; waves and slices become work; HANDOFF
"Already fixed" becomes decision; HANDOFF "Traps" becomes policy; LESSONS and
resource limits become decision and constraint; docs/experiments notes become
observation and evidence with watches; CONFORMANCE becomes milestone acceptance
plus observation. Generated views under docs/generated are the single reading
surface; the source markdown is retired to legacy citations. Historical
milestones are imported with source { kind legacy } so D-028 exempts their old
evidence commits from the descendant-commit gate.

**Context.** Planning lived in RUST_JXL_ENCODER_ROADMAP.md, JPXL/docs HANDOFF, PLAN and CONFORMANCE, and about twenty-five dated docs/experiments notes, all hand maintained and drifting. AKR makes the plan typed, checkable and generated.

**Consequences.** Agents propose and revise records and log papercuts instead of editing HANDOFF.md; wave commits become ledger writes. Renaming the namespace later rewrites every key, so it is fixed here.

## jpegxl-rs.decision.modular-lean-default

### Revision 1 — Modular default effort is the lean level 1; the full search is opt-in

`active` · `@jpegxl-rs.decision.modular-lean-default/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-cli/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/**"`

Effort::DEFAULT for the lossless modular path is Effort::MIN (level 1): one predictor, no split search, no per-leaf refinement, no palette/squeeze trials, coarse sampling stride, collapsed tree. The full pre-ramp search is retained verbatim at level 7 -- a byte-identical density anchor pinned by the effort_7_budget_is_the_pre_ramp_search test -- and levels 8-9 add finer stride and deeper search for density chasing. Effort is expanded once at the plan_for stage boundary into a ModularSearchBudget (Encoder-plan1.md 12), never re-checked in a kernel.

**Context.** The full search was measured to be chaff on the photo corpus: byte-identical output to level 1 at ~16x the wall time (jpegxl-rs.assessment.modular-effort-lean-default). Quality is preserved unconditionally because every level is exact-lossless.

**Consequences.** Default encodes are 4.6-16.9x faster on photos with byte-identical output (verified: .agent/scratch/effort-ramp-2026-08-10/verify_default_flip.ps1). Flat/paletteable content encodes a few percent larger by default (measured 3.7% on a synthetic screenshot) unless a higher effort is selected. This default-output change is deliberate but validated only on a limited corpus; a broader real-world UI/line-art corpus should confirm the tradeoff before any method is deleted (as opposed to demoted).

## jpegxl-rs.decision.opt-p-wide-rayon-deps

### Revision 1 — wide and rayon are feature-gated default dependencies for Opt-P

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.decision.opt-p-wide-rayon-deps/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/**"` · topic `opt-p-wide-rayon-deps`

The encoder optimization track may depend on the `wide` (portable SIMD)
and `rayon` (work-stealing pool) crates. Both are optional Cargo features
named `simd` and `parallel`, enabled by default on jpxl-core (simd),
jpxl-encode, jpxl-encode-policy, and jpxl-cli. Builds with
--no-default-features remain pure-scalar and std::thread-only. Contract A
holds across thread counts for section emission; SIMD kernels may use
Contract B float semantics relative to scalar builds and stay decode-valid.

**Context.** Approved during Opt-P leaf-SIMD work after coarse section parallelism landed.

## jpegxl-rs.decision.optimization-determinism-contract

### Revision 1 — Contract A for structural optimization; bounded Contract B for quality policy

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.decision.optimization-determinism-contract/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-bitstream/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-entropy/**"`

Default to Contract A for optimization changes: same source and options produce identical codestream bytes across thread counts, scheduling, and scalar versus optimized integer/bitstream paths. Structural refactors (BitWriter bulk path, plan Arc-sharing, coefficient arenas, scratch reuse, Rayon section encoding, integer SIMD) must prove byte-identical output. Contract B permits deliberate quality-policy changes after a recorded corpus gate. Phase 5G's target-rate AQ/quant_lf gate required matched achieved rate, no Butteraugli regression in 12 representative cells, at least 7.5% observed Butteraugli improvement in every cell, RMSE improvement in every cell, and disclosed SSIMULACRA2 regression bounded to 4.5 points. Phase 5I's active-EPF gate separately requires matched achieved rate, no Butteraugli regression in 12 cells, at least 0.6% observed Butteraugli improvement in every cell, RMSE and Butteraugli-pnorm3 improvement in every cell, and any SSIMULACRA2 regression disclosed and bounded to 0.05 points. Future Contract B changes require another explicit revision naming their bounds.

**Context.** VarDCT RD ties are sensitive to tiny float differences. Wide and hand SIMD can change NaN patterns and wrapping. The project already requires software-defined float conversion without fast-math for the reference pair. Phase 5G deliberately changed target-rate quantization policy. Phase 5I deliberately activates decoder restoration by signalling one EPF step and a uniform Sharpness 7 grid; this changes reconstructed pixels without changing coefficient decisions.

**Consequences.** Every structural PR needs scalar-vs-optimized and 1-vs-N-thread byte equality tests where applicable. Float kernel and RD-search work may not claim Contract A without proof. Phase 5 target-rate quality policies may be promoted only while their recorded corpus evidence satisfies the separately stated Butteraugli, RMSE, achieved-rate, pnorm3, and SSIMULACRA2 bounds. The observed SSIMULACRA2 tradeoffs remain explicit guardrails for later work.

## jpegxl-rs.decision.optimization-ordering

### Revision 1 — Optimization order: structure, then parallel, then SIMD

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.decision.optimization-ordering/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-bitstream/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-core/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/**"` · topic `optimization-ordering`

Within the encoder optimization pass, implement in this order: (1) separate
Modular and VarDCT benchmarks plus multiplicity counters; (2) remove repeated
full-frame work, deep plan clones, and per-varblock allocation; (3) replace
known-bad algorithms (bit-at-a-time writer, dense DCT32 fallback when factored
scalar exists, brute-force LZ only if hot); (4) reshape hot scalar loops for
the compiler; (5) coarse group and section parallelism with a single resource
policy; (6) explicit SIMD only on remaining leaf kernels; (7) LTO and PGO last.
Do not start with a general SIMD or Rayon sweep.

**Context.** Advisor static assessment. Aligns with correctness-before-speed (scalar before parallelism before SIMD).

## jpegxl-rs.decision.optimization-pass-opened

### Revision 1 — Open the encoder optimization pass under AKR

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.decision.optimization-pass-opened/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/**"` · topic `optimization-pass-opened`

Begin the encoder optimization pass now that M1-M8 exist. PLAN/AGENTS language
that deferred SIMD and Rayon for the scalar reference phase remains the default
outside this track; work on this track may introduce coarse parallelism and
leaf SIMD only after the measurement foundation and structural multiplicity
fixes land, and only under correctness-before-speed and forbid-unsafe-by-default.

**Context.** VarDCT M1-M8 and Modular density work (slice 19+) are feature-complete enough for a performance baseline. PERFORMANCE.md still has no rows. An external advisor assessment is captured as jpegxl-rs.assessment.encoder-static-optimization.

**Consequences.** Optimization work is planned as jpegxl-rs.track.encoder-optimization milestones. Density-pin vs cjxl becomes a Modular metric under the foundation milestone, not an excuse to skip benches.

## jpegxl-rs.decision.read-u32-wraps

### Revision 1 — read_u32 wraps mod 2^32, it does not error

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.decision.read-u32-wraps/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-bitstream/**"` · topic `read-u32-overflow`

Per 18181-1 B.2.2, read_u32 computes (offset + v) Umod (1 << 32): it wraps with
wrapping_add and never returns Overflow on offset + payload. Regression test
u32_offset_plus_payload_wraps_mod_2_pow_32. Do not harden this back into an error.

**Context.** Recovered from HANDOFF "Already fixed" (2026-08-02). The original scaffold returned Overflow; the fix carries a clause citation.

## jpegxl-rs.decision.retire-performance-md

### Revision 1 — Retire PERFORMANCE.md as plan-of-record for performance

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.decision.retire-performance-md/1` · scope `path ".agent/scratch/**"`, `path "JPXL/docs/**"` · topic `performance-docs-authority`

JPXL/docs/PERFORMANCE.md is no longer the plan-of-record for performance
baselines, measurement rules, or profiling results. Authority is split:

- Durable claims (baseline rules, bench entry points, summary observations,
  decisions): AKR records under jpegxl-rs.policy.performance-baseline-rules,
  jpegxl-rs.policy.jpxl-bench-entry-points, and jpegxl-rs.observation.preopt-*
  (and successors).
- Full raw run logs, flamegraph artifacts, HOTSPOTS/PROVENANCE: .agent/scratch/
  (not pruned by akr build). Current ladder:
  .agent/scratch/preopt-baseline-2026-08-06.md; current flamegraphs:
  .agent/scratch/flamegraphs/preopt-2026-08-06/.

PERFORMANCE.md remains only as a short stub pointing at those AKR keys and
scratch paths. Do not re-accumulate tables or rules in the markdown file.
Frozen experiment writeups may still go in JPXL/docs/experiments/ when an
experiment report is warranted.

**Context.** PERFORMANCE.md duplicated material that already lived as AKR observations and was drifting from scratch logs. AGENTS.md living-docs discipline prefers small generated views over hand-maintained performance tables.

**Consequences.** Opt-F acceptance and work language that required PERFORMANCE.md baseline rows must be revised to AKR observations + baseline-rules policy. Agents update observations and scratch, not long tables in PERFORMANCE.md.
